captures.q: What are the arguments in “EA-CORRESPONDENCE-OPENAIRE-CTO-02 v0.1: No Logs, Full Synch — 13–16 October 2026 exchange with Paolo Manghi (OpenAIRE CTO)” by Lee Sharks (Alexanarch deposit #1685, AXN:06FB)? Ground your answer in a reading of the text itself.
captures.description: THE OPENAIRE CTO CORRESPONDENCE ON CHATGPT, SIGNED OUT, AT THE RECORD PAGE'S OWN QUESTION: the answer reconstructs the three messages with their times, the two removal pathways, the changelog's blacklist figures, the Space Ark case with its 410 limitation, the successor-identifier question and Manghi's 'thank you for the recommendations', the duty of traceable departure in the deposit's words, and the five concepts of §7.3 at their deposits. It leaves out the account termination at Zenodo that the thread concerns, the 12 July notice that made the Space Ark the prospective test, the moderation mirror and OpenAIRE's quoted commitments; it gives two of the four requests, replaces the position table and mechanism ledger with a table of its own, and closes on six disclaimers. Its only source chip is 'Goodreads +1'.

atoms.evidence: The central argument of Lee Sharks's “No Logs, Full Synch” (#1685)
This distinction matters because the central argument does not depend on proving which mechanism removed the Space Ark.
1. The documentary argument: what OpenAIRE actually says
The deposit connects its documentary findings to concepts developed elsewhere in the Alexanarch archive.
An infrastructure that removes an entity it once served owes the public a record that the entity was there and left.
Importantly, Sharks acknowledges a limitation: the Zenodo HTTP 410 response was not included in the two formal October capture files. It was confirmed in the later 18 October re-probe.
Primary text: Lee Sharks, EA-CORRESPONDENCE-OPENAIRE-CTO-02 v0.1, deposit #1685 , reproduced under the title above.
